newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast power pressured by moderate demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast power pressured by moderate demand.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the northeastern corner of the country generally finished flat to lower versus Wednesday's levels amid moderate spot demand in the region due to seasonal weather.

Although temperatures have been in 20s Fahrenheit during off-peak hours this week, there appeared to be ample coal and nuclear generation to meet demand during those periods without the need to switch on high-cost oil and natural gas plants.
"I think it's weather rather than gas," said a Houston trader when asked about which factor drove the Northeast market today.
While Henry Hub natgas futures finished lower today on profit-taking, swing physical gas prices rose to mid-$3.60 to mid-$3.70 per million British thermal units, up roughly 30 cents from Wednesday.
At the utility receipt point in the New York City area, swing gas values were assessed near $4.30 in late trading.
"They probably won't have an impact until next week," a Northeast trader said.
In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity for Friday was quoted near $21.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), lower than a range of $22.00-$24.00 on Wednesday.

Some market participants said western New York prices fell in line with weaker values in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool. Western New York generators had been selling power into northern PJM because of more attractive prices.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Friday talked in the $14.00-$15.00 range, compared Wednesday's quote near $14.00.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Friday was assessed again at $26.00-$28.00 and off-peak, non-firm power for Friday stayed at $17.00-$18.00.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Friday at the Northeast Utilities border was notationally assessed near $32.00-$33.00, compared with $30.00-$31.00 on Wednesdsay.
Despite the lack of deals, peak-hour scheduling was said to be restricted at the NU border on Friday, thus bolstering next-day prices, marketers said.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Thursday delivery to the NU border was again pegged near $21.00.
